claims: The Artemis II mission successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego at 8:07 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II mission was a 10-day mission around the moon.
The Artemis II crew consisted of four astronauts.
The Artemis II crew safely returned to Earth.
The Artemis II mission broke records for the farthest human journey from Earth.
The Artemis II crew included NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis II crew successfully completed their lunar flyby mission.
The Orion capsule touched down in the Pacific Ocean.
The Artemis II astronauts were safely extracted by U.S. Navy personnel following the splashdown.
The Artemis II mission is a crewed flyby mission.
The Artemis II mission does not involve landing on the moon.
Landing on the moon is planned for future Artemis missions.
